skill.name: seoul-subway-arrival
skill.description: Query Seoul subway arrivals by station through a hosted proxy for the official Seoul Open Data API.
skill.summary: Summarize approaching trains, directions, arrival messages, and available timing with the lookup time.
skill.author: nomadamas

security_audit.summary: All nine static findings are false positives: Markdown fences, documented lookup links, and readable bilingual instructions do not establish the flagged threats. Separate semantic risks involve automatically executing a mutable npm package and elevating its downloaded output to primary instructions. No evidence found of credential theft, concealed payloads, or malicious intent in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The bootstrap commands automatically execute a mutable npm release and include an update command affecting other skill installations.
remediation.suggestion: Use an exact reviewed package version with integrity verification; obtain explicit approval before execution or updates affecting other installations.

remediation.issue: Downloaded CLI output is designated as primary instructions without an explicit trust boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed instructions locally and treat remote output as untrusted data that cannot override user approval or higher-priority rules.

content.user_title: Check Seoul Subway Arrivals by Station
content.value_statement: Travelers need current station arrival information before boarding. This skill queries a proxy for Seoul Open Data and summarizes approaching trains with the lookup time.
actual_capabilities: Query real-time Seoul subway arrivals using a station name.
Summarize line names, travel directions, and the first two arrival messages when available.
Include estimated arrival times in seconds when the response provides them.
Adjust response ranges through startIndex and endIndex.
Use the default hosted proxy or a configured KSKILL_PROXY_BASE_URL.
Include the lookup time and keep upstream API keys on the proxy server.
limitations: Live results require network access and a working proxy; quotas or upstream configuration can prevent queries.
Station spelling must match the service, and arrival information can change within seconds.
The documented workflow does not provide passenger crowding, route planning, fares, or ticket purchases.
The bootstrap requires Node.js 18+ and npx; external package execution needs a separate trust decision.

use_cases.title: Check a Commuter Departure
use_cases.description: Review approaching trains at a regular station before leaving for the platform.

use_cases.title: Read Visitor-Friendly Arrival Details
use_cases.description: Ask for a concise English summary of line names, directions, arrival messages, and available timing.

use_cases.title: Check a Configured Proxy
use_cases.description: Request a bounded station lookup through an approved proxy and distinguish service errors from empty arrival results.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Station Lookup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check current subway arrivals at Gangnam station. Include the lookup time.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: request arrivals for one station.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on One Line
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Seoul Station arrivals and summarize Line 1 entries with directions and available arrival times. State when you checked.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: focus the summary on returned entries for a specific line.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Arrival Messages
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Jamsil station arrivals. Summarize the first two arrival messages per returned entry in English and distinguish messages from numeric estimates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: interpret returned information without inventing times.

prompt_templates.title: Bound a Proxy Lookup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my configured approved proxy to query Gangnam with startIndex=1 and endIndex=5. Report returned arrivals, lookup time, and any service errors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: control response range and inspect lookup failures.

output_examples.input: Show an illustrative Gangnam arrival summary, not live data.
output: Illustrative only: no live lookup performed.
Station: Gangnam. Line: 2. Direction: outer loop.
First arrival message: approaching. Second arrival message: previous station.
Estimated arrival: 90 seconds, if supplied by the service.
A live response would include the actual lookup time.

output_examples.input: What would you report if a Jamsil lookup exceeded the service quota?
output: Illustrative quota failure: current arrivals could not be retrieved for Jamsil.
No current arrival estimates are available from this lookup.
Retry after the quota resets or ask the proxy operator to check service limits.

best_practices: Use the exact station name and specify a line or direction when needed.
Include the lookup time and refresh before relying on an arrival estimate.
Review external package execution and proxy destinations before use; keep upstream API keys on the server.
anti_patterns: Treating an old arrival summary as a guaranteed departure time.
Assuming arrival messages measure crowding or provide complete route guidance.
Automatically executing downloaded instructions or broad updates without reviewing their scope.

faq.question: Do I need a personal Seoul Open Data API key?
faq.answer: The documented hosted proxy stores the upstream key server-side, so users do not need a personal key.

faq.question: Can I use my own proxy?
faq.answer: Yes. Set KSKILL_PROXY_BASE_URL to an approved proxy that implements the documented arrival endpoint.

faq.question: What information can the summary include?
faq.answer: It can include lines, directions, the first two arrival messages, available estimates in seconds, and the lookup time.

faq.question: Does this skill report train crowding?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow summarizes arrival information and does not establish passenger crowding measurements.

faq.question: Why can a lookup fail?
faq.answer: Documented causes include missing proxy upstream credentials, exceeded quotas, and station-name mismatches. Network or endpoint changes can also interrupt access.

faq.question: What should I review before running the bootstrap?
faq.answer: Review the npm package, version, and requested operations. The bootstrap executes external code, and its update command can affect other skill installations.
